files.description: Meta-ADR — Status: approved at Step 03 (commit 715014a) under all four canonical sign-offs; links to eleven content ADRs + three autonomous-factory documents. Serves as the sign-off envelope for the eleven content ADRs (FR-001..FR-010 and FR-019). Sixth reviewer round 2026-05-29: aligned the Consequences §:109 bullet with the round-5 #2 C8 reframing — replaced the obsolete claim that C8 enumerates the ten ADRs as `stable` consumer-shipped surface with the corrected `internal` normative-reference classification (consumers inherit the architectural baseline via the C7/C8 contract surface and the consumer-overlay parameter mechanism, not via mirroring of the ADR files themselves, which are pruned at consumer init); this also resolves the meta-ADR's internal contradiction between :109 (claimed `stable` mirroring) and :113 (correctly stated 'ADRs are not mirrored per existing convention') (codex P2 round-6 #2). Seventh reviewer round 2026-05-29: fixed the SECOND occurrence of the obsolete `stable` C8-classification claim in the § Context (§:21) — round 6 only corrected the Consequences bullet at :109 but the same `stable` instruction to #339 C8 remained in the Context paragraph; rewritten to instruct C8 to enumerate the ten ADRs as `internal` normative references with the same Category (a) inheritance-mechanism preamble pointer (codex P2 round-7 #1). Tenth reviewer round 2026-05-30: cascaded ten→eleven across § Context (load-bearing decisions list now enumerates C7 emission mechanism), § Decision Drivers, Option A/B/C/D titles + bodies, § Decision sentence (twelve ADRs = eleven content + this meta-ADR), § Consequences (eleven Phase 0 architectural decisions; C8 enumerates the eleven ADRs; rollback-dependency bullet), § References (added FR-019 c7-emission-mechanism row; reciprocal-#339 bullet now mentions the C7 emission-mechanism sealed rule), and the Mermaid fan-out diagram (added A11 node + two outbound edges to #333 phase-boundary emission and #336 webhook-side emission).

FR-001 — LLM model router policy (three-tier router). Status: approved from inception under meta-ADR envelope. Eighth reviewer round 2026-05-30: added a Model identifier resolution paragraph to § Decision making explicit that the table identifiers (`claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-haiku-4-5`) are family/version names and the orchestrator MUST resolve each to the deployed gateway model ID via the per-instance LiteLLM access configuration declared by #339 Contract C8 FR-014; documents that the blueprint instance's deployed gateway today exposes the three sanctioned models as the `-data-hub-europe`-suffixed aliases (EU + ZDR posture per FR-004), and that this indirection bounds the FR-008 rotation surface to the family/version pair regardless of consumer-side alias naming. Surfaced by the empirical LiteLLM probe documented in the FR-008 round-8 explainer.
FR-002 — Persona-skill contract. Status: approved from inception under meta-ADR envelope.
FR-003 — Trigger authorization model. Status: approved from inception under meta-ADR envelope.
FR-004 — Sovereignty + ZDR posture; cites #339 NFR-SEC-001 verbatim per NFR-SEC-001 (prohibits factory-side egress allowlist content). Status: approved from inception.

FR-005 — Separation of duties at factory velocity; cites #339 NFR-SEC-001 verbatim per NFR-SEC-002 (factory-bot exact-string equality on GitHub login; no substring/regex/display-name heuristics). Status: approved from inception. Amended 2026-05-29 (Step 06 follow-up) with § Satisfaction paths — Path 1 multi-author (default) + Path 2 solo-operator (alternative, gated by `solo_operator: true` in contract.yaml + canonical attestation comment with five-item checklist); Option E (rejected) added; Consequences extended; `sealed` classification preserved (mode-selection from a fixed blueprint-defined path-set is not parameterization). Reviewer-round update 2026-05-29: added a prominent For-#336-implementers callout at the head of § Satisfaction paths so implementers cannot miss the two-code-path requirement (Claude review observation #5).

FR-006 — Reject-rerun cap (cap=2; factory-escalated label semantics). Status: approved from inception. Fourth reviewer round 2026-05-29: the rerun-cap-hit C7 emission was rewritten to use the valid C7 enum value `outcome: rejected` (the rerun trigger is rejected) with `rejection_reason: rerun-cap-exceeded` as a non-required extension field per C7's `additionalProperties: true` allowance (codex P2 round-4 #1); the matching Consequences bullet was updated to reflect the new outcome+reason pair.

FR-007 — Per-ticket wall-clock + cost ceiling (90 min / $15 USD per work item, per child for decomposed parents — Q-1 Option A). Status: approved from inception. Fourth reviewer round 2026-05-29: the ceiling-hit C7 emission was rewritten to use the valid C7 enum value `outcome: human-handoff` (the pause requires human action to clear via `agent-resume`) with `pause_reason: ceiling-hit` as a non-required extension field per C7's `additionalProperties: true` allowance (codex P2 round-4 #2).

FR-008 — Reviewer model heterogeneity (rotation rule). Status: approved from inception. MDX braces escaped at Slice 8 for docs-build compatibility. Eighth reviewer round 2026-05-30: enforcement-point split correction — empirical probe of the deployed LiteLLM gateway (https://garagedoor.api.dev.sit.sys.odj.cloud) confirmed the issued virtual key is scoped to `llm_api_routes` only (admin endpoints refuse with `Virtual key is not allowed to call this route. Only allowed to call routes: ['llm_api_routes']`), making the original 'LiteLLM gateway MUST enforce the rotation by reading the C7 stream' Enforcement clause infeasible against the deployed instance and architecturally awkward (LiteLLM is a stateless routing proxy, not a C7-event-aware orchestrator). Split enforcement across (a) orchestrator-side picker in #333 (queries C7 for step05.model, selects the pair opposite, passes the chosen model on the LiteLLM request) and (b) C7-ingestion audit invariant in #336 (pairs step08 with step05 on the same `work_item_id`, asserts model inequality, emits `outcome: rejected` + `rejection_reason: rotation-violation` on violation with `factory-escalated` label + PR comment). Updated Decision Drivers bullet 2, Decision Enforcement paragraph, Implementer paragraph, Consequences bullets 1–3 (was 1), and the Phase 1 implementers reference line accordingly. Rotation rule, pairings table, and Haiku exclusion are unchanged; only the enforcement location moves. `sealed` extensibility classification preserved — the rotation rule itself remains sealed; only the implementation locus is corrected. Cross-reference Model identifier resolution paragraph added to § Decision (after the pairings table) delegating per-instance gateway-ID resolution to the FR-001 ADR's matching paragraph; ensures the rotation invariant holds at the family/version layer regardless of consumer-side alias naming.

FR-009 — Triage size threshold (4-class table: small / medium / large-decomposable / escalate — Q-2 Option A). Status: approved from inception. Third reviewer round 2026-05-29: the `escalate` routing rule's C7 emission was rewritten to use the valid C7 enum values `phase: intake` + `outcome: human-handoff` (replacing the schema-invalid `outcome: escalate-class-blocked`); the specific blocking reason is now described as an optional extension field per C7's `additionalProperties: true` allowance (codex P2 #4). Fourth reviewer round 2026-05-29: the Consequences C7 row was rewritten to stop storing triage classes in the `outcome` field — triage emissions now carry `outcome: success` (when the classification function runs to completion) with the triage class itself carried as a `triage_class` extension field per C7's `additionalProperties: true` allowance (codex P2 round-4 #4).

FR-010 — Light decomposition policy (boundary types; fan-out <=5; refusal->escalate; parent ## Integration Acceptance Criteria per #339 C4). Status: approved from inception. MDX braces escaped at Slice 8 for docs-build compatibility. Fourth reviewer round 2026-05-29: the bot-tick-block C7 emission was rewritten to use the valid C7 enum value `outcome: rejected` (the bot's tick attempt is rejected) with `rejection_reason: integration-criteria-bot-tick-blocked` as a non-required extension field per C7's `additionalProperties: true` allowance (codex P2 round-4 #3).

FR-019 — C7 emission mechanism. Status: approved (Option A — two-emitter rule: orchestrator (#333) for phase-boundary events, webhook handler (#336) for GitHub-observable events; LiteLLM, OpenHands, workspace pods, personas, and skills MUST NOT emit C7 events). Authored round 10 (2026-05-30) after empirical pushback exposed an LLM-hallucination risk in any 'persona-emits-C7' design: persona output would have to carry envelope fields and have direct durable-bus access, both of which can silently regress on prompt drift. The ADR pins the contract that skills declare a structured-output schema (a fenced ```yaml jsonschema``` block in each SKILL.md per FR-002 — authoring deferred to #333) which the orchestrator validates before emitting; this collapses the emission surface to two deterministic services that cannot drift on LLM prompts. Idempotency rule pins `event_id = sha256(work_item_id|phase|rerun_round|emitter)` so duplicate emission from retry is harmless. Local exemption preserved per the existing C7 local-exemption clause. Sealed under FR-017(b) item 8 in design-contracts.md. Twelfth reviewer round 2026-05-30: rewrote the § Decision orchestrator-emission-responsibilities table framing to preface that each phase boundary emits EXACTLY ONE atomic C7 event whose identification fields are populated before persona invocation and whose outcome fields are populated after persona exit + structured-output validation, and reframed the table rows as outcome-decision rules (not separate emissions); idempotency derivation cited verbatim to anchor the one-event invariant (codex P2 round-12 — one-event ADR framing). Aligns the ADR text with the round-11 spec.md FR-019 'EXACTLY ONE atomic event' clarification.

FR-012 + FR-013 — Instrumentation plan: primary + guardrail metrics, per-`owner_team` shape, source-of-truth field per metric, durable-bus emission rule (STACKIT Managed RabbitMQ stream queues with Strimzi-Kafka fallback per Q-5), 13-month retention parity with #334 LogMe WORM (Q-4). Reviewer-round update 2026-05-29: named #334 explicitly as the implementation owner of the sidecar emitter, and expanded the #334 reference line to include LogMe WORM at the 13-month SOC 2 retention floor (Claude review observations #2 and #3). Second reviewer round 2026-05-29: re-anchored the primary-metric source-of-truth onto GitHub Issues / PR events (the `agent-ready` `labeled` event + `pr.merged_at`) because the C7 nine-field schema only represents persona-phase emissions and cannot model label/merge events (codex P2 #3); applied the same re-anchor to the two reviewer-wall-time guardrail rows (human sign-off comments are not C7-emitted per design-contracts.md § C7 emission rule); tightened the first-review-rejection-rate row wording to use C7's actual fields (`persona`, `outcome: rejected`, `rerun_round: 0`); corrected the per-`owner_team` derivation line to reference C7's `owner_team` field (not `actor_team`) snapshotted on the first `phase: intake` event. Third reviewer round 2026-05-29: switched RabbitMQ queue type from `quorum` to `stream` (`x-queue-type: stream`) — log-structured offset-addressable storage that natively satisfies C7 Replayability for new-subscriber catch-up (codex P2 #5); rewrote the C7-to-RabbitMQ mapping table accordingly; reclassified LogMe as long-tail forensic audit beyond the bus retention window rather than as the in-bus replay path; corrected the Data Sources C7 row to remove the misleading 'every label application' claim — label applications are GitHub events, not C7 events (codex P2 #6). Tenth reviewer round 2026-05-30: flipped the Data Sources C7 row owner attribution from 'factory runtime (#335)' to 'orchestrator service (#333) for phase-boundary events; webhook handler (#336) for GitHub-observable events' per the new FR-019 ADR; flipped the Phase 1 implementers footer to add #333 (orchestrator service — phase-boundary C7 emission + persona/skill discovery + FR-008 reviewer-rotation picker) and to narrow #335 to 'runtime target only; NOT a C7 emitter' and to add 'webhook-side C7 emission' to #336.

FR-014 — Pre-factory baselines: measurement window 2026-04-17->2026-05-28 (commit df7595c), n=100 merged PRs (Q-6 Option A), four baselines (lead time, reviewer wall-time, formal rejection rate transparently NOT MEASURABLE, defect rate proxy), per-`owner_team` breakdown row, calibration trigger declared. Reviewer-round update 2026-05-29: reworded the § Sample-Size Caveats line to make explicit that n=100 is the verified full population of merged PRs in the 41-day window (via `gh pr list --limit 300`), not an API pagination cap (Claude review observation #4). Fifth reviewer round 2026-05-29: corrected the forward-comparable-factory-metric line to use the C7 sealed enum value `outcome: rejected` (it previously used the schema-invalid `outcome: reject`), with an inline note pointing readers at the sealed enum definition in `design-contracts.md` § Contract C7 (codex P2 round-5 #1). Sixth reviewer round 2026-05-29: fixed the SECOND occurrence of `outcome: reject` in the § Calibration Trigger (§:105) — round-5 #1 only corrected the §:57 instance; same C7 sealed-enum spelling correction (now `outcome: rejected`) with the same inline note pointing readers at the sealed enum definition `success | rejected | retried | human-handoff` in `design-contracts.md` § Contract C7 (codex P2 round-6 #1).

FR-015 — Triage + decomposition data feed: 100-row machine-readable Markdown table with `### Sample Size` subsection per Q-7 Option A; retrospective-hypothetical caveat present; consumed by #338 as directional evidence.

FR-011 — Two-layer routing per CODEOWNERS last-match-wins semantics: gate-1 sign-off teams (@sbonoc/factory-{product,architecture,security,operations}) + gate-2 bounded-context teams (@sbonoc/factory-context-{factory,infra,docs,governance}); Q-3 Option A. Zero `@your-org/...` placeholders; AGENTS.md ownership preserved by tail-block re-anchor. Reviewer-round update 2026-05-29: appended an additional tail-block re-anchor (broad-to-narrow ordering) for `/docs/blueprint/architecture/**`, `/.agents/**`, `/docs/blueprint/autonomous-factory/**`, the ADR-issue-33* glob, and the four new autonomous-factory deliverables — defeats the line-118 `/docs/blueprint/**` docs catch-all so the specialized owners actually win per last-match-wins (codex P1 + P2 inline comments). Eleventh reviewer round 2026-05-30: (a) added `@sbonoc/factory-architecture` co-owner to the `/docs/blueprint/architecture/decisions/ADR-issue-33*` final-matching line so factory ADRs preserve gate-1 architecture sign-off in addition to gate-2 factory-context-factory ownership (codex P2 round-11 — ADR ownership); (b) added a new tail re-anchor block with six per-artifact narrower rules (`/specs/**-issue-33*-factory-**/{spec,pr_context,discovery,architecture,plan,tasks}.md`) that re-name the gate-1 sign-off team (Product for spec/pr_context/discovery, Architecture for architecture/plan/tasks) alongside the gate-2 factory-context-factory team — defeats the gate-2 `/specs/**-issue-33*-factory-**` rule that would otherwise drop the gate-1 sign-off owners on factory work-item specs (codex P2 round-11 — Gate 1 owners on factory specs). Twelfth reviewer round 2026-05-30: added `@sbonoc/factory-context-factory` co-owner to the four narrower autonomous-factory deliverable re-anchors (`design-contracts.md`, `instrumentation-plan.md`, `pre-factory-baselines.md`, `triage-decomposition-data-feed.md`) — preserves the C6 / FR-011 two-layer routing on these final matching lines so factory bounded-context expertise is not dropped by last-match-wins (codex P2 round-12 — factory ownership on autonomous-factory deliverables).
